newsitem.title: DENMARK: Warring Danish bikers fire missile at police cells.
newsitem.headline: Warring Danish bikers fire missile at police cells.

text.p: An anti-tank missile slammed into a Danish police cellblock on Sunday, wounding a member of a motorcycle gang held there, in what appeared to be the latest salvo in a gang war which has killed eight people.

Police in the town of Koege said the rocket, fired from a nearby main road, struck the cell window of a prominent member of the Bandidos -- locked in a vendetta with the Hells Angels -- but did not explode.

"The rocket smashed a window pane and created a shockwave but at the moment it does not look as if it exploded," Detective Inspector Bruno Juul-Pedersen said in the town, 35 km (22 miles) southwest of Copenhagen.
The shoulder-fired missile was similar to one which ploughed into a party at Hells Angels' Copenhagen headquarters last October, killing a gang member and a woman guest.
Police would not name the wounded man, said to be recovering from relatively minor injuries in Koege hospital, but the Danish news agency Ritzau said that he was one of several Bandidos in the jail.

The two gangs, offshoots of U.S. bike clans, have been battling over turf in Denmark, Finland, Norway and Sweden since shortly after the Bandidos established themselves in the region in the summer of 1993.
The feud claimed its first life in February 1994, when a member of the Hells Angels-affiliated Rednecks died in a gunfight with Bandidos in the Swedish port of Helsingborg.
Two Bandidos died over the next two years, in Sweden and Finland and in March 1996 the fighting took on a new intensity.

Gunmen outside Copenhagen International airport shot dead Danish Bandidos leader Uffe Larsen and wounded three of his companions as they waited to meet fellow-members returning from a visit to Helsinki.
A Copenhagen court, sitting in the tightest security ever seen in Denmark, jailed two Hells Angels for the killing in December.
A Danish Bandido was shot dead near the Norwegian city of Drammen in July.

The most recent incident was the killing of Hells Angel Kim Svendsen on January 11 in the provincial town of Aalborg in what police believe was an act of revenge for the serious wounding of a Bandido in the town a month earlier.
